A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sampling framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampler evaluations on synthetic distributions, Bayesian logistic regression, and the phi4 model, plus runtime measurements and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, runtime measurements, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The MultALMC and MultCDiff dynamics, heavy-tailed variant, and numerical procedures are retained. New main-text Algorithm 1 summarizes v1 Algorithm 2, whose detailed implementation remains as v2 Algorithm 3; it introduces no different sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian and Student’s t mixtures, Rings, Funnel, double-well distributions, Ionosphere, Sonar, and phi4 model. Appendix dimensionality studies and test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain SMC, AIS, ULMC, PT, DiGS, RDMC, and SLIPS. The optimal-initialization SLIPS comparison in Table 7 and the Laplace/SLIPS comparisons for phi4 also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises RDMC’s reported terminal times: for example, Rings changes from 0.10 to -log(0.85), and Ionosphere and Sonar from 0.10 to -log(0.95). These are different settings, not equivalent rounding. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The heavy-tail comparisons, dimensional scaling analyses, overdamped-versus-underdamped comparison, and sensitivity studies for SROCK stages, scale separation, and sampling steps are retained. Figures 3–4 redisplay existing ablations from v1 Tables 12–15.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 removes the statement that baseline hyperparameter selection used 30 random seeds, retaining only the 4096-sample count. This reduces reporting detail without establishing fewer runs. Benchmark seed counts and ablation uncertainty values remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported outcomes in Tables 1–2, 7, and 9–11 and Figures 1–2 are unchanged. The plotted means and error bars in v2 Figures 3–4 match v1 Tables 12–15; these are redisplayed results, not new findings.

T1.justification: v2 adds regularity assumptions for the score identity in Section 2.1, corrects the averaged SDE’s noise term from sqrt(2)dt to sqrt(2)dBt in Section 2.2, and squares the metric derivative in Section 4.2’s action definition, restoring consistency with Appendix A. The principal theorems and appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims about training-free multiscale sampling, avoiding nested MCMC, underdamped acceleration, heavy-tailed extensions, convergence guarantees, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of acceleration, heavy-tail performance, and hyperparameter sensitivity remain unchanged. Sections 4 and 6 and Appendices C and F retain the same limitations concerning strong convexity, heavy-tailed convergence analysis, and manual tuning.

D1.justification: Appendix D replaces the anonymous code-access pointer with a named GitHub repository. v2 explicitly clarifies scalar/isotropic mass and friction parameters, corrects the GPU designation from GTX to GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, and revises RDMC hyperparameter values. These are documentation changes; changed code or hardware use is not established.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to neural diffusion samplers, learning-free nested samplers, and proximal samplers are retained. Citation punctuation and bibliographic formatting changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain intact. v2 makes local explanatory additions around the score identity and Gaussian conditioning, adds a pointer to the simplified algorithm, and edits terminology, punctuation, and author information.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting with different typography, title/author layout, spacing, and float placement throughout. It adds a compact main-text algorithm display and replaces four ablation tables with two paired error-bar figures, including logarithmic step-count axes. This substantially revises presentation while preserving the underlying results.

improvement.justification: Correcting the action definition and Brownian term removes mathematical inconsistencies, while the main-text algorithm summary and implementation clarifications improve readability. These limited gains outweigh reduced tuning-seed disclosure and less convenient access to exact ablation values after conversion to plots. The empirical evidence and central theoretical results remain unchanged.
